title: SYSK Gets Weird Playlist: Doppelgängers: Hey you, you're me!
summary: Playlist episode on doppelgangers (unrelated lookalikes). The hosts trace the word from Jean Paul's 18th-century novel Siebenkäs and folklore such as seeing your double three times as a death omen, then review literary and historical doubles (Poe's William Wilson, Dostoevsky's The Double, Lincoln's mirror vision, Shelley, Goethe). They discuss photographer Francois Brunel's "I'm Not a Lookalike!" series, a Spanish study by Manel Esteller finding genetic similarity among doppelganger pairs, Tegan Lucas's one-in-a-trillion facial measurement estimate, the Ryanair seat doppelganger encounter, and the Las Vegas pool encounter. They cover the fusiform gyrus face-recognition region, facial recognition bias and wrongful arrests (Nijeer Parks), how lookalikes work as celebrity doubles and political decoys (Kim Jong-un, Saddam Hussein's double Latif Yahia, Stalin, M.E. Clifton James posing as Montgomery). The episode closes with listener mail from Elkie about Ashkenazi Jewish matchmaking, responding to the Kissin' Cousins episode.
topics: I'm Not a Lookalike photo series

segments.title: Playlist preview
segments.summary: Josh introduces the playlist episode on doppelgangers as the final entry in the playlist.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts open with the Labor Day edition and mention a photographer's doppelganger series.

segments.title: Francois Brunel's doppelganger photo series
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Montreal photographer Francois Brunel and his 20-year series I'm Not a Lookalike!, in which he photographs found and submitted doppelganger pairs in his studio.
topics: I'm Not a Lookalike photo series

segments.title: Origin of the word doppelganger
segments.summary: Josh explains the German word meaning double goer or double walker, coined by Jean Paul in his novel Siebenkäs at the end of the 18th century, and notes the T dropped from the spelling.

segments.title: Doppelganger folklore and omens
segments.summary: The hosts describe older superstitions, including the belief that seeing your doppelganger three times meant death, and Norse folklore about the Varduger, a spirit that arrives before you.

segments.title: Doppelgangers in literature
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Poe's William Wilson and Dostoevsky's The Double, plus the Paul Rudd series Living With Yourself.

segments.title: Doppelgangers in TV comedy and historical accounts
segments.summary: The hosts mention doppelganger plots in TV comedy, then begin historical accounts, including Lincoln's mirror vision and Mary Todd's prediction.

segments.title: Historical doppelganger anecdotes
segments.summary: The hosts discuss John Donne, Percy Bysshe Shelley's doppelganger before his sailing death, the Catherine the Great impostor, and Goethe's doppelganger on the road.

segments.title: Brunel's photos and the genetics study
segments.summary: The hosts return to Brunel's photos and describe a Spanish study by Manel Esteller at the Carreras Leukemia Research Institute, which found doppelganger pairs share genes, though epigenetics and microbiomes were essentially random.

segments.title: Genetics and epigenetics of lookalikes
segments.summary: Josh explains why identical twins differ through the epigenome, and the hosts recap that doppelgangers were no closer than random strangers in epigenetics and microbiome.

segments.title: Facial similarity probability study
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Tegan Lucas's 2015 study of 4,000 U.S. Army anthropometric face scans, which estimated a one-in-a-trillion chance of two faces matching across eight measures, and its implications for facial recognition false positives.

segments.title: What counts as a doppelganger
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the lack of an agreed definition, how shortcuts like hats and beards make people look alike, and a face-swap meme of George W. Bush and Dick Cheney.

segments.title: How we register faces
segments.summary: Josh describes a 1977 study suggesting people register faces by eyes, then mouth, then nose, and the whole-face gestalt that makes lookalikes easy to confuse.

segments.title: Ryanair seat doppelganger and Las Vegas pool
segments.summary: The hosts recount Neil Douglas meeting his doppelganger in his Ryanair seat, the estimated 74,000 lookalikes, and Sean McArdle's doppelganger in a Las Vegas pool.

segments.title: Face perception and the fusiform gyrus
segments.summary: Josh describes the fusiform gyrus as a brain region specialized for faces, and Chuck describes an experiment where electrical stimulation changed how participants perceived their own faces.

segments.title: Blind participants and face-specific brain activity
segments.summary: Josh describes a follow-up study in which blind-from-birth participants touching 3D face models activated the fusiform gyrus, while cube models did not.

segments.title: Facial recognition bias and wrongful arrest
segments.summary: The hosts discuss facial recognition AI performing worse on people of color and the wrongful arrest of Nijeer Parks in New Jersey, attributed to training data bias.

segments.title: Lookalikes as celebrity doubles
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh joke about being a Lizzo doppelganger and discuss jobs for lookalikes, including photo doubles and body doubles where size and skin tone matter.

segments.title: Political decoys and body doubles
segments.summary: The hosts discuss political decoys, including Kim Jong-un, Saddam Hussein's double Latif Yahia from The Devil's Double, Stalin's doubles, and M.E. Clifton James posing as Bernard Montgomery in WWII deception.

segments.title: Film recommendations and wrap-up of topic
segments.summary: The hosts mention Operation Mincemeat and a Swedish series on the assassination of Olof Palme, then Josh wraps up the doppelganger episode.

segments.title: Listener mail: Ashkenazi matchmaking
segments.summary: Listener Elkie writes in response to the Kissin' Cousins episode about genetic screening and matchmaking in her insular Ashkenazi Jewish community.

segments.title: Listener mail call to action
segments.summary: Josh thanks Elkie and explains how to send listener email to the show.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck closes with the iHeartRadio production credit and directs listeners to podcast apps.
